correlates.name: Mycoplasma pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 19-year-old army recruit; several in his barracks are coughing. Ten days of gradually worsening headache, malaise, low-grade fever without chills and a dry, persistent cough; still training. T 38.0 C, HR 88, RR 18, SpO2 97%; fine crackles scattered over both lungs.
correlates.workup: Chest film: patchy bilateral interstitial infiltrates that look worse than the patient. Gram stain: no organisms. Cold agglutinin titer raised; LDH up and haptoglobin low (IgM-driven hemolysis). Pleural effusion in 10-20%.
correlates.management: Macrolide (azithromycin), doxycycline or a fluoroquinolone; beta-lactams fail because the organism has no cell wall. Macrolides are the choice in pregnancy and children. Usually self-limited.

correlates.name: Klebsiella pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 56-year-old man with diabetes who drinks a fifth of vodka daily; found passed out 4 days ago. Fever, shortness of breath and cough bringing up thick, sticky, blood-stained sputum. T 39.1 C, HR 112, RR 28, SpO2 89%; dullness and bronchial breath sounds at the right apex.
correlates.workup: Chest film: dense right upper lobe consolidation with an early cavity. Sputum Gram stain: plump gram-negative rods with thick capsules; culture: mucoid, lactose-fermenting colonies on MacConkey agar. CT may show a liver collection too.

correlates.name: Typical community-acquired pneumonia (outpatient)
correlates.presentation: Healthy 41-year-old teacher; no recent hospital stay or antibiotics. Three days of fever, cough with yellow sputum and left-sided pain on deep breaths. T 38.4 C, HR 96, RR 20, BP 124/78, SpO2 96%; eating and drinking; dullness, crackles and loud breath sounds at the left base.
correlates.workup: Chest film: left lower lobe consolidation (CT only if the film is unclear). Sputum Gram stain and culture rarely done; blood cultures are reserved for admitted patients; no organism identified in most cases.
correlates.management: Treat at home with amoxicillin, doxycycline or a macrolide. With heart, lung or kidney disease, cancer treatment or alcoholism: amoxicillin-clavulanate or a cephalosporin plus a macrolide, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone.

correlates.name: Aspiration pneumonia
correlates.presentation: 74-year-old man 2 months after a left-hemisphere stroke; coughs and chokes when he drinks, and vomited during an upper endoscopy 3 days ago. Now fever, tachypnea and cough with purulent sputum. T 38.7 C, HR 104, RR 26, SpO2 90%; coarse crackles and dullness at the right base.
correlates.workup: Chest film: right lower lobe infiltrate (the right main bronchus is steeper). Sputum culture: more than one organism, aerobes outnumbering anaerobes, mixed oral flora. Early chemical injury from gastric acid, then bacterial infection.
correlates.management: Blood and sputum cultures, then anaerobic coverage: clindamycin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, or metronidazole plus a beta-lactam. Prevent: speech and swallow evaluation, head of bed at 30-45 degrees, minimal sedation, oral care.

correlates.name: Lung abscess
correlates.presentation: 58-year-old man with heavy drinking, badly decayed teeth and a blackout 3 weeks ago. Two weeks of fever, cough with large amounts of foul-smelling purulent sputum, chest pain and a 4-kg weight loss. T 38.4 C, HR 100, SpO2 94%; finger clubbing; crackles over the right upper back.
correlates.workup: Chest film: 5-cm thick-walled cavity with an air-fluid level in the right upper lobe. Sputum: mixed oral anaerobes; acid-fast smear negative. Biopsy: suppurative destruction around the cavity; a fibrotic rim means chronicity.
correlates.management: Prolonged antibiotics with anaerobic coverage (clindamycin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, or metronidazole + a beta-lactam), effective in most. In an older patient, rule out an underlying carcinoma (found in 10-15%).
